commands.command: design: ExportSink/ExportFileWriter trait + FilesystemSink (repopact-mobile-acquisition/src/sink.rs), export_tree + scan_source_fingerprint (src/export.rs), SourceStatus + compare_fingerprints (src/divergence.rs), ExportBounds (src/bounds.rs)
commands.summary: New platform-neutral export primitives mirroring Checkpoint A's import-side layering exactly: Rust owns traversal order, path validation (reuses reject_unsafe_relative_path), bounds, cancellation, and progress; a sink implementation owns only 'how does a directory/file actually get created here'. export_tree walks a FilesystemSource (the app-private repository/ directory, already-trusted content) and writes through any ExportSink. scan_source_fingerprint performs a read-only, non-writing re-listing (no file bytes opened) for the source-divergence check, producing the same bounded SourceFingerprint shape captured at import time so the two are directly comparable -- never a claim of cryptographic proof, consistent with Decision 0057's existing fingerprint fidelity.

commands.command: repopact-mobile-saf: new Rust bridge functions (pick_export_directory, create_export_root, delete_document, pick_export_archive_destination, upload_completed_archive) + AndroidExportSink/AndroidFileWriter implementing ExportSink/ExportFileWriter against the real SAF plugin; Kotlin plugin additions (pickExportDirectory, createExportRoot, createChildDocument, writeDocumentFromStagingFile, deleteDocument, createExportArchive)
commands.summary: Mirrors the import-side AndroidSafSource/SafAcquisitionPlugin pattern exactly. AndroidExportSink performs zero path validation/bounds/collision logic of its own -- all of that is export_tree's job; it only tracks each created directory's document URI by relative path so a nested entry's parent is always known. A file's bytes are staged to a local, app-private per-file temp file first and uploaded to the real SAF destination only in ExportFileWriter::finish (never a byte-by-byte streamed write, matching the JSON-only plugin channel constraint already documented for imports). createExportRoot performs its own case-insensitive existing-child check before calling DocumentsContract.createDocument, returning a typed conflict rather than ever letting a provider silently rename/merge.

commands.command: Operational note: an intervening emulator (qemu) crash and restart occurred between the Checkpoint D session's compaction boundary and its resumption
commands.summary: Not a RepoPact defect: the host emulator process itself crashed (GPU/graphics-backend related, per its own crash log) between turns of this session and was restarted with an explicit swiftshader software-GPU backend for stability. All previously-registered workspaces and their registry entries survived this restart intact, EXCEPT the 'repopact-mutation-fixture' workspace (Checkpoint C's mutation-carrying workspace), whose entire app-private directory was absent after the restart -- most likely because the emulator's virtual disk had not flushed that specific write to its backing image before the abrupt qemu termination, a host-storage-layer failure outside anything Decision 0057's own atomic-rename/registry-corruption guarantees claim to cover (those guarantees are about the app's own write ordering, not about a lower-level disk image surviving an ungraceful process kill). This does not invalidate the mutation-carrying export proof captured immediately above (in this same evidence record) and earlier in this session, before the crash -- those hashes were captured and recorded from the live, then-still-present workspace.
